pr_title: Bug 3905 factor file.apply method removes the factor file first row
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
This PR fixes the `FactorFile.Apply` method. Previously, it removed the first row of the `FactorFile` object after applying a new event.

Also the Apply method now can handle duplicated events.

Finally, This PR adds support for exponential notation in QuantQuote's factor files.

<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Closes #3905 

#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
First row in factor file is important because the factor files are read backwards.

No.

issue_context.title: FactorFile.Apply method removes the factor file's first row
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
The `FactorFile.Apply` method should be able to add or update new events, without modifying the factor file structure.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
When new events are added with the `Apply` method, the first row of the factor file is removed.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
Fix the logic when parsing `FactorFileRow` into events.

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->
Add the following asserts:
```cs
Assert.True(actual.First().Date == new DateTime(1998, 01, 02),
                $"Factor file first row changed from 1998-01-02 to {actual.First().Date:yyyy-MM-dd} after applying new event");
```
to the [apply method tests](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Tests/Common/Data/Auxiliary/FactorFileTests.cs#L198).

#### System Information
<!--- Required for Bugs. Include any system specific information, such as OS. -->
Windows 7

review_comments: Hmm, does the `e+` actually mean it's inf? I suppose by convention we don't serialize using scientific notation, but perhaps more correctly we could define inf as `"inf"` or anything larger than, for example, `1e6`. If we are going to say that _all_ scientific notation equates to inf, then we'll want to document this behavior somewhere since it's unexpected. For example, a value such as `1.23e+2` would be flagged unexpectedly as an inf value

Exponential notation is treated as `inf` is because of the loss of precision. In all cases, the significant  part has fewer decimals than the needed for a correct representation, E.g., 1.6e+6 when the correct factor is  1562500. I'll add that as a comment.

Worth notice that there are only 6 factor files with exponential notation, 10 cases with `inf`, and 2 cases where both cases are present.
